thread.title: Stock Market Rises On Strength In Internet Stocks | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stock Market Rises On Strength In Internet Stocks | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market rebounded midday Thursday from the previous session's negative reversal. Internet stocks did the heavy lifting, as the Nasdaq regained the 8,000 level.
X Small caps lagged, holding 0.1% above the break-even line. The Nasdaq sprinted 0.9% higher, while the large cap S&P 500 added 0.6%. Blue chips were mostly up as Apple 's ( AAPL ) 2% gain lifted the Dow 0.5%. JPMorgan initiated coverage on Apple with an overweight rating and 272 price target.
Volume rose on the NYSE but stepped back on the Nasdaq.
Since late August, the Nasdaq has bobbed above and below the 8,000 level. In the meantime, the S&P 500 is testing the 2915 area, which also has provided resistance since late August.

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) popped 1.5% in brisk volume. Latin America's MercadoLibre ( MELI ) advanced 4% in strong volume. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) headed toward its fourth gain in a row, rising 1.2% in above-average turnover. Facebook ( FB ) climbed 1.6% in average volume.
Airline stocks ascended, but most of the stocks are well off their highs. Exceptions include Southwest Airlines ( LUV ), up 1.5% and only 5% off its high; and Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), up 1.5% and only 3% off its high.
A stream of fairly significant financial data flowed into the market's scope Thursday.
Financial Reports The third take on second quarter GDP came in at 4.2%, matching the previous reading but a tick below the expected 4.3% level, according to Econoday .
First-time jobless claims were essentially in line, rolling in at 214,000 vs. the Street's consensus estimate of 215,000.
Durable goods orders for August were more than twice as much as estimated. Orders ballooned 4.5%, trouncing views for 2.2%. Core capital goods, a gauge of business spending plans, fell 0.5%, a bad miss. Analysts expected a 0.4% increase.
Still, the year-over-year reading on core capital goods is up 7.4%, according to Reuters .
